Just then, out of nowhere, I heard what sounded like a scream.
Then the old school building grew noisy somehow.
It seemed the missing student had been found.
The moment that happened, Nao stood up.
What had become of the missing student?
Judging from the strange atmosphere inside the old school building, I thought there was no way he was all right.
It wouldn't be so bad to see what had become of someone who'd played such a stupid game.
I went out into the hallway with Nao.{p}

...I see.
Same as me.
I mean, you don't know what kind of person the thief is.
If they had a knife or something, you'd be the one in danger.
And unless you catch them red-handed, you're stuck if they play dumb.
I fought down the urge to burst out and stayed still in that cramped cleaning closet.
And then...
Right about when I figured the one I took for the thief had reached the middle of the classroom, their presence suddenly just vanished.{p}

...Oh right, it was still before noon.
I think that's what went through my head.
Ahaha, even though that was no time for it.
The blinding light wasn't coming in from the windows.{p}
rows.65:2a88:
At the next break, Kawahara went up to the roof.
After making sure nobody was around, he started to open the textbook he'd hidden under his uniform.
It was really windy that day.
To keep whatever was inside the textbook from blowing away, he moved into a corner, out of the wind.
He was just nervously trying to peek inside, when...
The door to the roof slowly opened, and he saw someone's shadow.
That silhouette wasn't a student's.
From the necktie flapping in the wind, he knew right away it was a teacher.
The teacher was far off, but seemed to be watching Kawahara closely.
You see, someone had told on him for acting strange.
So the teacher had followed him up there.
The teacher came closer, one step at a time.
The teacher's mouth clearly looked as if it had something to say.
And the teacher's eyes were fixed on the textbook in Kawahara's hands.
With every step closer, the shadow grew bigger.
